name: AirZeta (2025)
description: Light gray-white fuselage; behind the wing a royal-blue field covers the aft fuselage, its front edge running from the crown at the fin's leading edge down and forward to the mid-side, then back to the belly; blue fin with the AirZeta mark (a red slanted bar over a white slanted block notched in blue); 'AIRZETA' in big wide royal-blue capitals over the forward fuselage; red winglets; a Korean flag on the aft fuselage.

logos.description: The AirZeta mark: two parallel slanted blocks leaning forward at the top, the upper a red parallelogram, the lower a white one whose upper-left part is notched in blue so the pair reads as a stylised Z; on the blue fin, high and aft.
A small South Korean flag on the blue aft fuselage under the fin's leading edge.

titles.style: Big wide geometric capitals in royal blue, heavy, the A's without crossbars' serifs and slightly leaning, across the forward main deck.

notes: Drawn from 747-400F HL7419 (left side, February 2026) and checked on HL7616 (September 2026) and HL7419's right side. Not every AirZeta freighter wears it yet: ex-Asiana 747s fly in all-white or in basic Asiana paint with titles removed (HL7620 'in basic Asiana scheme', April 2026; HL7646 white with a black 'CARGO', September 2026; HL7421 white with a gray swoosh and 'CARGO', May 2026). Those aren't tagged: there is no file for those plain schemes. The callsign became QUANTUM SKY on 2026-07-01 (Wikipedia, uncited). Re-checked 2026-11-15 on HL7419 (2026-02-16) and HL7616 (2026-09-25): AIRZETA leans ~14° (the I and T stems), not 5°; its place and length (0.233) agree; the blue aft field's edge is two straight diagonals meeting at a point by the window line: the points along them replaced by their ends.
history: Added with the cargo divisions (2026-11-13): Air Incheon rebranded as AirZeta on 2025-08-01 when it took over Asiana Airlines' cargo division.
